RQ1 Step 1: Data understanding, cleaning and the processed dataset

What drives the real cost per m² of new houses across districts?

while True: learn(), Group 8, STAT462

2026-11-07

source(file.path(proj_root, "R", "utils_data.R"))
library(knitr)

# ---- Settings for this notebook (change here, not further down) ------------
MIN_HOUSES   <- 5        # minimum new houses for a district-quarter to be modelled
TRAIN_LAST_Y <- 2019     # train = up to 2019Q4, test = 2020Q1 onwards (as pitched)
BASE_YQ      <- c(2026L, 2L)   # express real dollars in June-2026-quarter dollars

1 What this notebook does

Research question 1 (slide 6 of the pitch): What drives the real cost per m² of new houses across districts? Models are trained on district-quarters up to 2019 and tested on 2020–2026 (Step 3).

Before modelling we need a single, clean, model-ready table with:

  • One row per district × quarter (67 territorial authorities, 1990Q2–2026Q2).
  • The response: the real consented value per m² of new houses, so that a 1995 quarter and a 2025 quarter are measured in the same dollars.
  • Candidate drivers (features) built from the consents data and placed alongside it.
  • Flags for the train/test split and for rows too small to trust.

This notebook builds that table in nine steps, checking each one, and saves it to data/processed/. Every later RQ1 notebook (EDA, models) starts from the saved file instead of from the 757 MB raw CSV.

2 Which data do we need?

2.1 The 13 files in the consents release

The two Stats NZ zips gave us 13 CSVs. Only some of them matter for RQ1:

File Used for RQ1? Why
Building consents by territorial authority (Monthly) Yes, main source The only file with district-level houses: count, value and floor area.
New dwellings consented per 1000 residents by territorial authority (Annual) Yes, a feature How fast a district is building relative to its population.
Building consents by region (Quarterly) Yes, a check Lets us confirm our district → region mapping adds up.
Building consents by region (Monthly) No Same as the quarterly file at a finer grain; no district detail.
Building consents by Auckland local board (Monthly) Not now Only needed if we split Auckland into its 21 boards.
Building consents by institutional sector / control (Monthly) No National only, no geography.
New dwellings by 2023 / 2026 SA2 (Monthly) Not now Dwelling counts only: no value or floor area, so no $/m².
Per 1000 residents by region / Auckland local board No Region or board level only.
Non-residential outliers, NZ percentage change No National series.

2.2 Data from outside the release

Consent values are nominal (in the dollars of the day) and include GST. To get a real cost we need a price index for building work. Stats NZ publishes one in a separate release:

  • Capital Goods Price Index (CGPI), Business price indexes: June 2026 quarter, quarterly, base Sep 2022 quarter = 1000. Downloaded into data/raw/external/cgpi/ from the Stats NZ release page (CSV zip). Two candidate series:
    • CEPQ.S611011A: Dwelling units (closest match to new houses)
    • CEPQ.S61101: Residential buildings (all residential)
    • We also keep CEPQ.S61102, Non-residential buildings, to deflate the non-residential feature.

We also need a district → region lookup, which no file provides. We wrote one by hand (data/reference/ta_region_concordance.csv; districts that cross a regional boundary go to the region holding most of their population) and check it against the regional file in section 6.

Nothing else is needed for a first model. Optional extras for later, if time allows: district house-price indices, land values, or population estimates.

3 Load the territorial authority table

The TA file is long-format (one row per series × month), 4.35 million rows. We read it with data.table::fread, which takes seconds rather than minutes.

ta_raw <- read_infoshare("Building consents by territorial authority (Monthly).csv",
                         keep_status = TRUE)
dim(ta_raw)
## [1] 4348384       9
ta_raw |> count(Status, name = "rows") |> kable(caption = "Row status")
Row status
Status rows
F 4348384

Observation. 4,348,384 rows; every one has status F (final), so none of the values we use will be revised in a later release.

3.1 Keep only the series RQ1 needs

There are 26 nested building types × 3 kinds of work × 3 measures. We take just the series we need and give each one a short variable name. Because the building types are nested (houses are inside dwelling units, which are inside residential buildings, …) we never add across them.

series_map <- tribble(
  ~var,             ~btype,                                          ~work,     ~measure,
  "houses_n",       "Houses",                                        "New",     "Number",
  "houses_m2",      "Houses",                                        "New",     "Floor area",
  "houses_val",     "Houses",                                        "New",     "Value",
  "dwell_n",        "Dwelling units",                                "New",     "Number",
  "apt_n",          "Apartments",                                    "New",     "Number",
  "retire_n",       "Retirement village units",                      "New",     "Number",
  "town_n",         "Townhouses, flats, units, and other dwellings", "New",     "Number",
  "resid_new_val",  "Residential buildings",                         "New",     "Value",
  "resid_alt_val",  "Residential buildings",                         "Altered", "Value",
  "nonres_new_val", "Non-residential buildings",                     "New",     "Value"
)
kable(series_map, caption = "Series taken from the TA file")
Series taken from the TA file
var btype work measure
houses_n Houses New Number
houses_m2 Houses New Floor area
houses_val Houses New Value
dwell_n Dwelling units New Number
apt_n Apartments New Number
retire_n Retirement village units New Number
town_n Townhouses, flats, units, and other dwellings New Number
resid_new_val Residential buildings New Value
resid_alt_val Residential buildings Altered Value
nonres_new_val Non-residential buildings New Value 
ta_month <- ta_raw |>
  inner_join(series_map, by = c("btype", "work", "measure")) |>
  select(area, period, var, value) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = var, values_from = value)

rm(ta_raw); invisible(gc())
dim(ta_month)
## [1] 30453    12

3.2 Check 1 — is the grid complete?

After pivoting, a missing series would show up as NA. We look at the 68 sub-national areas (67 TAs + “Area Outside Territorial Authority”) from April 1990.

sub_nat <- ta_month |> filter(area != "New Zealand")

tibble(
  areas          = n_distinct(sub_nat$area),
  first_month    = min(sub_nat$period),
  last_month     = max(sub_nat$period),
  months         = n_distinct(sub_nat$period),
  rows           = nrow(sub_nat),
  expected_rows  = n_distinct(sub_nat$area) * n_distinct(sub_nat$period),
  missing_values = sum(is.na(sub_nat |> select(-area, -period)))
) |> kable()
areas first_month last_month months rows expected_rows missing_values
68 1990.04 2026.08 437 29716 29716 0

Observation. The grid is complete: every area has every month from 1990.04 to 2026.08 and no value is missing. Zeros are real zeros (no houses consented that month), not gaps.

3.3 Check 2 — does the building-type hierarchy add up?

Dwelling units should equal houses + apartments + retirement units + townhouses/flats. Stats NZ rounds, so we allow a difference of 1.

sub_nat |>
  mutate(diff = dwell_n - (houses_n + apt_n + retire_n + town_n)) |>
  summarise(rows_checked = n(),
            rows_off_by_more_than_1 = sum(abs(diff) > 1),
            max_abs_diff = max(abs(diff))) |>
  kable()
rows_checked rows_off_by_more_than_1 max_abs_diff
29716 0 0

3.4 Check 3 — do districts add up to New Zealand?

sum_check <- sub_nat |>
  group_by(period) |>
  summarise(across(c(houses_n, houses_m2, houses_val), sum), .groups = "drop") |>
  inner_join(ta_month |> filter(area == "New Zealand") |>
               select(period, nz_n = houses_n, nz_m2 = houses_m2, nz_val = houses_val),
             by = "period")

sum_check |>
  summarise(months = n(),
            count_mismatch = sum(abs(houses_n - nz_n) > 1),
            m2_mismatch    = sum(abs(houses_m2 - nz_m2) > 1),
            value_mismatch = sum(abs(houses_val - nz_val) > 1000)) |>
  kable()
months count_mismatch m2_mismatch value_mismatch
437 0 0 0

Observation. Both checks are exact: dwelling units equal the sum of their four sub-types in every district-month, and the districts (plus the area outside any TA) add up to the New Zealand total for count, floor area and value in all 437 months. The file is internally consistent, so we can use the house series as published without repairing anything.

4 Monthly → quarterly district frame

Monthly district figures are noisy: a small district may consent 3 houses one month and none the next. Following the pitch, the unit of analysis is the district-quarter. We:

  1. drop the national total and the “Area Outside Territorial Authority”,
  2. sum the three months of each quarter (sums of counts, $ and m², not averages of ratios), and
  3. keep only complete quarters (all 3 months present), which removes the partial 2026Q3 (Jul–Aug).
ta_q <- sub_nat |>
  filter(area != "Area Outside Territorial Authority") |>
  mutate(year    = period_year(period),
         quarter = month_quarter(period_month(period))) |>
  group_by(ta = area, year, quarter) |>
  summarise(months = n(),
            across(all_of(series_map$var), sum),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  filter(months == 3) |>
  select(-months) |>
  mutate(yq = yq_label(year, quarter), t_index = yq_index(year, quarter)) |>
  arrange(ta, t_index)

tibble(districts = n_distinct(ta_q$ta),
       quarters  = n_distinct(ta_q$yq),
       first     = min(ta_q$yq), last = max(ta_q$yq),
       rows      = nrow(ta_q)) |> kable(caption = "The district-quarter frame")
The district-quarter frame
districts quarters first last rows
67 145 1990Q2 2026Q2 9715

Observation. 67 districts × 145 quarters = 9,715 rows, matching the 9,715 in the pitch.

5.1 Check 4 — do our district sums reproduce the regional file?

The regional quarterly file is compiled from the true geography of each consent, so a district that straddles a regional boundary (e.g. Taupō, Waitaki, Tararua, Rangitīkei) will create small differences. Large differences would mean a district is in the wrong region.

reg_q <- read_infoshare("Building consents by region (Quarterly).csv") |>
  filter(btype == "Houses", work == "New", measure == "Number", adjust == "Actual") |>
  transmute(region = area,
            year = period_year(period),
            quarter = month_quarter(period_month(period)),
            reg_houses_n = value)

region_check <- ta_q |>
  group_by(region, year, quarter) |>
  summarise(our_houses_n = sum(houses_n), .groups = "drop") |>
  inner_join(reg_q, by = c("region", "year", "quarter")) |>
  group_by(region) |>
  summarise(quarters       = n(),
            our_total      = sum(our_houses_n),
            file_total     = sum(reg_houses_n),
            pct_difference = 100 * (our_total - file_total) / file_total,
            .groups = "drop") |>
  arrange(desc(abs(pct_difference)))

save_tab(region_check, "t01_region_check") |> kable(digits = 2,
  caption = "New houses 1990-2026: sum of our districts vs the regional file")

The lookup is correct; the small differences are the boundary-straddling districts and do not matter for a grouping feature.

6 From nominal to real $/m²

6.1 The price index

cgpi <- fread(file.path(paths$raw_cgpi, "business-price-indexes-june-2026-csv.csv"),
              select = c("Series_reference", "Period", "Data_value"),
              colClasses = list(character = "Period")) |>
  as_tibble() |>
  filter(Series_reference %in% c("CEPQ.S611011A", "CEPQ.S61101", "CEPQ.S61102")) |>
  mutate(year = period_year(Period), quarter = month_quarter(period_month(Period))) |>
  select(series = Series_reference, year, quarter, index = Data_value) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = series, values_from = index) |>
  rename(cgpi_dwell = `CEPQ.S611011A`, cgpi_resid = `CEPQ.S61101`,
         cgpi_nonres = `CEPQ.S61102`) |>
  arrange(year, quarter)

# one row per quarter, and our whole frame is covered
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(cgpi[c("year", "quarter")]))
missing_q <- anti_join(distinct(ta_q, year, quarter), drop_na(cgpi), by = c("year", "quarter"))
nrow(missing_q)   # should be 0
## [1] 0
base <- cgpi |> filter(year == BASE_YQ[1], quarter == BASE_YQ[2])

p_cgpi <- cgpi |>
  filter(year >= 1990) |>
  mutate(date = year + (quarter - 1) / 4,
         `Dwelling units (S611011A)`        = cgpi_dwell / base$cgpi_dwell,
         `All residential (S61101)`         = cgpi_resid / base$cgpi_resid) |>
  pivot_longer(c(`Dwelling units (S611011A)`, `All residential (S61101)`),
               names_to = "series", values_to = "index") |>
  ggplot(aes(date, index, colour = series)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("#2a6f97", "#e07a1f")) +
  labs(title = "Building costs have roughly quadrupled since 1990",
       subtitle = "Capital Goods Price Index, rescaled so June 2026 quarter = 1",
       x = NULL, y = "Index (2026Q2 = 1)", colour = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
save_fig(p_cgpi, "fig01_cgpi")

cor(cgpi$cgpi_dwell, cgpi$cgpi_resid, use = "complete.obs")
## [1] 0.9995751

Decision. We use Dwelling units (CEPQ.S611011A), because it prices the type of building in our response. The two series are almost identical, so this choice will barely change the results.

6.2 GST

Consent values include GST, and GST rose from 12.5% to 15% on 1 October 2010. Without a correction, every district’s $/m² jumps by 1.15 / 1.125 = +2.2% in 2010Q4 for a purely tax reason. We therefore:

  1. remove the GST of the day: value / (1 + GST rate at the time),
  2. deflate with the CGPI to June-2026-quarter prices, and
  3. add back today’s 15% GST, so the numbers stay comparable to the GST-inclusive figures in the pitch.

\[ \text{real\_cost\_m2} = \frac{\text{value}}{\text{floor area}} \times \frac{1}{1+\text{GST}_t} \times \frac{\text{CGPI}_{2026Q2}}{\text{CGPI}_t} \times 1.15 \]

ta_q <- ta_q |>
  left_join(cgpi, by = c("year", "quarter")) |>
  mutate(
    gst          = gst_rate(year, quarter),
    real_factor  = (1.15 / (1 + gst)) * (base$cgpi_dwell / cgpi_dwell),
    nominal_cost_m2 = if_else(houses_m2 > 0, houses_val / houses_m2, NA_real_),
    real_cost_m2    = nominal_cost_m2 * real_factor,
    # real values of the other $ series (non-residential uses its own index)
    resid_alt_val_real  = resid_alt_val  * real_factor,
    nonres_new_val_real = nonres_new_val * (1.15 / (1 + gst)) * (base$cgpi_nonres / cgpi_nonres)
  )

6.3 Sanity check against the pitch

The pitch said national new-house $/m² went up ×4.7 in nominal terms between 1991 and 2025, but only about +14% in real terms. We recompute the national series from our districts.

nz_year <- ta_q |>
  group_by(year) |>
  filter(n_distinct(quarter) == 4) |>
  summarise(nominal = sum(houses_val) / sum(houses_m2),
            real    = sum(houses_val * real_factor) / sum(houses_m2),
            houses  = sum(houses_n),
            avg_m2  = sum(houses_m2) / sum(houses_n), .groups = "drop")
invisible(save_tab(nz_year, "t02_nz_annual_cost_m2"))

nz_year |> filter(year %in% c(1991, 2000, 2010, 2019, 2025)) |>
  mutate(year = as.character(year)) |>
  kable(digits = 0, format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
        caption = "New Zealand new houses: $/m² (real = June-2026 dollars, GST 15%)")
New Zealand new houses: $/m² (real = June-2026 dollars, GST 15%)
year nominal real houses avg_m2
1991 681 2,749 12,380 153
2000 835 2,628 15,394 192
2010 1,391 3,006 13,066 216
2019 2,217 3,271 22,269 194
2025 3,226 3,311 16,635 178 
p_nz <- nz_year |>
  pivot_longer(c(nominal, real), names_to = "basis", values_to = "cost_m2") |>
  ggplot(aes(year, cost_m2, colour = basis)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(nominal = "#9aa5b1", real = "#2a6f97"),
                      labels = c("Nominal", "Real (June 2026 $)")) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::dollar) +
  labs(title = "Once inflation is removed, the cost of a square metre has moved far less",
       subtitle = "Consented value per m² of new houses, New Zealand",
       x = NULL, y = "$ per m²", colour = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
save_fig(p_nz, "fig02_nz_nominal_vs_real")

Observation. Nominal growth 1991→2025: ×4.74. Real growth: 20.5%. Most of the headline increase is general building-cost inflation. In real terms the cost per m² fell slightly through the early 1990s, then rose fairly steadily from 1996 to about 2019 and has been roughly flat since.

The pitch quoted +14% real growth; we get a bit more because we (a) use the dwelling-unit index rather than all-residential, (b) deflate quarter by quarter rather than by annual averages, and (c) remove the 2010 GST step, which lowers early-year values relative to recent ones. The conclusion is the same: the 4.7× nominal rise is almost all inflation. What is left over (the real level, and especially how it differs between districts) is what RQ1 tries to explain. The +14% quoted on slide 6 of our pitch becomes about +20% under this method.

7 Features: candidate drivers of cost

Each feature is computed per district-quarter. We avoid any feature built from house value, because value is the numerator of the response and would leak the answer into the predictors.

Feature Meaning Why it might drive cost
avg_house_m2 floor area ÷ number of new houses Bigger houses spread fixed costs (kitchen, bathrooms, consenting) over more m²
log_houses_n log of new houses consented Scale: builders in busy markets may be cheaper (or demand pushes prices up)
multiunit_share share of new dwellings that are not stand-alone houses Urban density / land scarcity
retire_share, apt_share retirement-village / apartment share of new dwellings Market type
dwell_per_1000 new dwellings in the 12 months to this quarter per 1,000 residents Building intensity relative to population (from 1996 only)
houses_yoy log change in houses vs the same quarter last year Demand pressure / boom-bust
log_resid_alt_real, log_nonres_real real value of residential alterations / new non-residential work Overall construction activity competing for builders
region, island, is_city, ta location Land, transport, labour and climate (e.g. insulation rules) differ by place
year, quarter, t_index time Trend and seasonality left after deflating
real_cost_m2_lag1, _lag4 the district’s own cost last quarter / a year ago Persistence; only for a forecasting version of the model 
per1000 <- read_infoshare("New dwellings consented per 1000 residents by territorial authority (Annual).csv") |>
  mutate(year = period_year(period), month = period_month(period)) |>
  filter(month %in% c(3, 6, 9, 12), area != "New Zealand") |>   # year ending at each quarter-end month
  transmute(ta = area, year, quarter = as.integer(month / 3), dwell_per_1000 = value)

stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(per1000[c("ta", "year", "quarter")]))
setdiff(unique(per1000$ta), unique(ta_q$ta))   # names should all match (expect none)
## character(0)
rq1 <- ta_q |>
  left_join(per1000, by = c("ta", "year", "quarter")) |>
  group_by(ta) |>
  arrange(t_index, .by_group = TRUE) |>
  mutate(
    avg_house_m2    = if_else(houses_n > 0, houses_m2 / houses_n, NA_real_),
    log_houses_n    = log(pmax(houses_n, 1)),
    multiunit_share = if_else(dwell_n > 0, 1 - houses_n / dwell_n, NA_real_),
    apt_share       = if_else(dwell_n > 0, apt_n / dwell_n, NA_real_),
    retire_share    = if_else(dwell_n > 0, retire_n / dwell_n, NA_real_),
    houses_yoy      = log((houses_n + 1) / (lag(houses_n, 4) + 1)),
    log_resid_alt_real = log1p(resid_alt_val_real),
    log_nonres_real    = log1p(nonres_new_val_real),
    # lagged response: only trusted when that quarter also had enough houses
    real_cost_m2_lag1 = if_else(lag(houses_n, 1) >= MIN_HOUSES, lag(real_cost_m2, 1), NA_real_),
    real_cost_m2_lag4 = if_else(lag(houses_n, 4) >= MIN_HOUSES, lag(real_cost_m2, 4), NA_real_)
  ) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(is_city   = str_detect(ta, " City$") | ta == "Auckland",
         log_real_cost_m2 = log(real_cost_m2))

Observation. Lags and the year-on-year change are computed before any rows are filtered out, so a lag always refers to the true previous quarter rather than the previous kept row.

7.1 Relative cost: each district compared with the rest of New Zealand

This response was added after the Step 2 EDA showed that time explains about 40% of the variation in real cost, and that 2020–2026 costs sit well above the training years.

RQ1 asks about differences across districts. A cleaner response for that question is a district’s cost relative to the rest of the country in the same quarter:

\[ \text{rel\_log\_cost\_m2} = \log(\text{district real \$/m}^2) - \log(\text{real \$/m}^2 \text{ of all other districts, same quarter}) \]

A value of +0.10 means “about 10% dearer than the rest of NZ that quarter”. The national level is computed leave-one-out (excluding the district itself). Otherwise Auckland, which has up to 40% of all houses in some quarters, would partly be compared with itself. We do the same for house size (rel_house_m2).

nat_q <- rq1 |>
  group_by(yq) |>
  summarise(nat_val_real = sum(houses_val * real_factor),
            nat_m2 = sum(houses_m2), nat_n = sum(houses_n), .groups = "drop")

rq1 <- rq1 |>
  left_join(nat_q, by = "yq") |>
  mutate(
    loo_cost_m2     = (nat_val_real - houses_val * real_factor) / (nat_m2 - houses_m2),
    loo_house_m2    = (nat_m2 - houses_m2) / (nat_n - houses_n),
    rel_log_cost_m2 = log_real_cost_m2 - log(loo_cost_m2),
    rel_house_m2    = log(avg_house_m2 / loo_house_m2)
  ) |>
  select(-nat_val_real, -nat_m2, -nat_n)

rq1 |> filter(houses_n >= MIN_HOUSES) |>
  summarise(mean_rel = mean(rel_log_cost_m2), sd_rel = sd(rel_log_cost_m2),
            sd_abs = sd(log_real_cost_m2)) |> kable(digits = 3)
mean_rel sd_rel sd_abs
-0.036 0.114 0.152

Observation. We keep both responses. log_real_cost_m2 asks “how expensive, in real terms?”, which mixes national time effects with district effects. rel_log_cost_m2 asks “how much dearer or cheaper than the rest of NZ at the same time?”, which isolates the district effect that RQ1 is about. Step 2 compares them.

8.2 Ratios from few houses are noisy

p_funnel <- rq1 |>
  filter(houses_n > 0) |>
  ggplot(aes(houses_n, real_cost_m2)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.25, size = 0.8, colour = "#2a6f97") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = MIN_HOUSES, linetype = 2, colour = "#c0392b") +
  scale_x_log10() +
  scale_y_log10(labels = scales::label_dollar(accuracy = 1)) +
  labs(title = "Districts with only a handful of houses give unreliable $/m²",
       subtitle = paste0("Each point is a district-quarter; dashed line = minimum of ",
                         MIN_HOUSES, " houses"),
       x = "New houses in the quarter (log scale)",
       y = "Real $/m² (log scale)")
save_fig(p_funnel, "fig03_funnel_small_counts")

Observation. The spread narrows as the number of houses grows (a “funnel”). Below about 5 houses a single unusual consent (a tiny cabin, a luxury build) dominates the quarter. We keep these rows in the full file but exclude rows with fewer than 5 houses from modelling. A sensitivity check with 10 can be run later by changing MIN_HOUSES at the top.

8.4 Shape of the response

p_resp <- kept |>
  select(`Real $/m²` = real_cost_m2, `log(real $/m²)` = log_real_cost_m2) |>
  pivot_longer(everything()) |>
  ggplot(aes(value)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 60, fill = "#2a6f97") +
  facet_wrap(~ name, scales = "free") +
  labs(title = "In real dollars the response is close to bell-shaped, with a slightly longer right tail",
       x = NULL, y = "District-quarters")
save_fig(p_resp, "fig04_response_distribution", height = 3.4)

Observation. Once inflation is removed, most of the skew disappears: the middle 98% of modelled rows lie between about $2,000 and $4,150 per m² (median about $2,800), with a slightly longer right tail and a few very low quarters from small districts in the early 1990s. Nominal dollars would have been strongly skewed, because they mix the price levels of different decades.

We will still model log(real $/m²) as the main response, because (i) effects of drivers on cost are naturally multiplicative (“10% more expensive”), so coefficients read as percentage effects, and (ii) it tames the remaining tails slightly. Trees and random forests don’t need this, but using the same response for every model keeps the comparison fair. Both versions are saved, so we can check in Step 3 whether it matters.

9 Train / test split

The split is by time, not random. All districts move together with the national building cycle, so a random split would put quarters from the same year in both sets and make the test score look better than it is.

rq1 <- rq1 |>
  mutate(split    = if_else(year <= TRAIN_LAST_Y, "train", "test"),
         in_model = houses_n >= MIN_HOUSES & !is.na(real_cost_m2))

split_tab <- rq1 |>
  group_by(split) |>
  summarise(period = paste(min(yq), "to", max(yq)),
            all_rows = n(),
            modelled_rows = sum(in_model),
            districts_modelled = n_distinct(ta[in_model]), .groups = "drop") |>
  arrange(desc(split))
save_tab(split_tab, "t03_split_sizes") |> kable(caption = "Train/test split")
Train/test split

  filter(in_model) |>
  count(year, split) |>
  ggplot(aes(year, n, fill = split)) +
  geom_col() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(train = "#2a6f97", test = "#e07a1f")) +
  labs(title = "Chronological split: train on 1990–2019, test on 2020–2026",
       x = NULL, y = "Modelled district-quarters", fill = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
save_fig(p_split, "fig05_train_test_split", height = 3.4)

Observation. The pitch’s 7,973 / 1,742 counts were for all district-quarters; after dropping rows with fewer than 5 houses the modelled counts are those in the table above. 2026 has only two quarters, and dwell_per_1000 starts in 1996, so the earliest training years will have that feature missing.

11 Summary of decisions

# Decision Reason
1 Main source: TA monthly file, new houses only Only file with district value + floor area
2 Unit = district-quarter, complete quarters only (1990Q2–2026Q2) Monthly counts too noisy; 2026Q3 is partial
3 Drop “Area Outside TA” and the NZ total Not districts
4 Remove GST of the day, deflate by CGPI Dwelling units, express in June-2026 $ incl. 15% GST Compare all years on one price basis, without the 2010 GST step
5 Model rows need ≥ 5 houses Ratios from very few houses are noise
6 Responses log(real $/m²) and relative cost rel_log_cost_m2 (raw also saved) Effects read as percentages; relative cost isolates differences between districts
7 No feature uses house value (lagged cost is saved but kept out of the main models) Avoid leaking the answer
8 Train ≤ 2019, test 2020–2026 Time-ordered validation, as pitched
9 Keep Auckland as one district Simple first; local boards are an option later

Next step (Step 2): exploratory analysis of the processed table: how real $/m² varies by district, region and time, and which features relate to it. That will guide which features go into the models (Step 3).

12 Appendix: helper functions

This notebook uses helper functions from R/utils_data.R, printed here so the document is complete on its own.

# =============================================================================
# R/utils_data.R
# Shared helpers for reading and reshaping Stats NZ data.
# Source this from any Rmd after the project root has been set:
#   source(file.path(proj_root, "R", "utils_data.R"))
# =============================================================================

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(data.table)
  library(tidyverse)
})

# ---- Paths (all relative to the project root) -------------------------------
paths <- list(
  raw_extracted = "data/raw/extracted",
  raw_cgpi      = "data/raw/external/cgpi",
  reference     = "data/reference",
  processed     = "data/processed",
  fig_rq1       = "outputs/figures/rq1",
  tab_rq1       = "outputs/tables/rq1"
)

# ---- Reading Stats NZ "Infoshare" long-format CSVs --------------------------
# Every Infoshare file has one row per (series x period). We read only the
# columns that carry information and give them short working names.
#
# Notes
# * `Period` MUST be read as text: as a number, "2025.10" becomes 2025.1,
#   which is indistinguishable from January.
# * integer64 is turned off so that large dollar values come back as doubles
#   (integer64 silently overflows on division).
read_infoshare <- function(file,
                           dir = paths$raw_extracted,
                           keep_status = FALSE) {
  cols <- c("Series_reference", "Period", "Data_value",
            "Series_title_1", "Series_title_2",
            "Series_title_3", "Series_title_4", "Series_title_5")
  if (keep_status) cols <- c(cols, "Status")

  dt <- fread(file.path(dir, file),
              select      = cols,
              colClasses  = list(character = "Period"),
              integer64   = "double",
              na.strings  = c("", "NA"),
              showProgress = FALSE)

  as_tibble(dt) |>
    rename(series  = Series_reference,
           period  = Period,
           value   = Data_value,
           area    = Series_title_1,
           btype   = Series_title_2,
           work    = Series_title_3,
           measure = Series_title_4,
           adjust  = Series_title_5)   # Actual / Seasonally adjusted / Trend (regional files only)
}

# ---- Period helpers ----------------------------------------------------------
# "YYYY.MM" -> integer year / month / calendar quarter
period_year    <- function(p) as.integer(substr(p, 1, 4))
period_month   <- function(p) as.integer(substr(p, 6, 7))
month_quarter  <- function(m) (m - 1L) %/% 3L + 1L

# Label like "2019Q3"
yq_label <- function(year, quarter) paste0(year, "Q", quarter)

# Sequential quarter index (1990Q1 = 1) - handy as a numeric time trend
yq_index <- function(year, quarter) (year - 1990L) * 4L + quarter

# ---- GST ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# Consent values are GST-inclusive. GST was 12.5% from 1 Jul 1989 to
# 30 Sep 2010 and 15% from 1 Oct 2010. Every month in our data is >= 1990,
# so only these two rates apply. Quarter boundaries line up with the change
# (2010Q4 starts on 1 Oct 2010), so a quarter-level rule is exact.
gst_rate <- function(year, quarter) {
  if_else(yq_index(year, quarter) >= yq_index(2010L, 4L), 0.15, 0.125)
}

# ---- Small display helpers ---------------------------------------------------
fmt_int <- function(x) format(round(x), big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE)
fmt_dol <- function(x) paste0("$", fmt_int(x))
fmt_pct <- function(x, d = 1) paste0(format(round(100 * x, d), nsmall = d), "%")

# ---- Figures -----------------------------------------------------------------
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
            theme(plot.title.position = "plot",
                  panel.grid.minor = element_blank()))

# Save a ggplot as PNG (for the report) and return it (so it also shows in the Rmd)
save_fig <- function(p, name, dir = paths$fig_rq1, width = 7, height = 4.2) {
  dir.create(dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  ggsave(file.path(dir, paste0(name, ".png")), p,
         width = width, height = height, dpi = 200, bg = "white")
  p
}

# Save a table as CSV (for the report) and return it
save_tab <- function(df, name, dir = paths$tab_rq1) {
  dir.create(dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  write_csv(df, file.path(dir, paste0(name, ".csv")))
  df
}
